prompt.context_jp: 健二の未亡人は 双子製菓の援助が必要だし ル･ソベールの ブランドネームやイメージ___ やはり利用価値がある
prompt.prompt_jp: ル･ソベールの ブランドネームやイメージ___ やはり利用価値がある
prompt.prompt_en: The executive is explaining why the acquisition is worthwhile. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks Le Sauveur's brand name and image as the topic the speaker is now commenting on — he's shifting focus to assess its value as a separate point from the widow's needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the brand name as new information being identified, but here it's already established in context and being evaluated. を doesn't fit because 利用価値がある is not a transitive verb phrase taking a direct object here.

contrast_examples.jp: ブランドイメージは価値がある。
contrast_examples.en: As for the brand image, it has value. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: ブランドイメージが崩れた。
contrast_examples.en: The brand image collapsed. (new event-focused subject)

prompt.context_jp: 健二の未亡人は 双子製菓の援助___ 必要だし
prompt.prompt_jp: 健二の未亡人は 双子製菓の援助___ 必要だし
prompt.prompt_en: What does the widow need? Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: With 必要 (an adjective-like state), the thing needed is marked with が. 未亡人は is the topic; 援助が is what she needs — presented as the specific item of need.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would create double-topic awkwardness and lose the 'specifically this is what's needed' focus. を can't appear with 必要だ, which is a stative predicate, not a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: I need money. (が marks the needed thing)

prompt.context_jp: 健二先生がいなくなっても 技術やレシピ___ 残っています
prompt.prompt_jp: 技術やレシピ___ 残っています
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke contrasts what's lost with what remains. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は carries contrastive force here: Chef Kenji is gone, BUT the techniques and recipes remain. The contrast with 健二先生がいなくなっても is the whole point.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report the existence of techniques as new info, losing the deliberate contrast Sōsuke is making to reassure the executives. に doesn't fit this subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 人はいないが、記憶は残る。
contrast_examples.en: The person is gone, but the memory remains. (contrastive は)
A recipe was there (I discovered). (new info が)

prompt.context_jp: 健二先生___ いなくなっても 技術やレシピは残っています
prompt.prompt_jp: 健二先生___ いなくなっても
prompt.prompt_en: In the subordinate clause about Kenji's absence, choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: In subordinate clauses (〜ても, 〜から, 〜時), the subject typically takes が, not は. The topic は is reserved for the main clause (技術やレシピは残っています).
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜ても clause would sound off and compete with the main-clause topic. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: Even if it rains, I'll go. (subordinate が)

prompt.context_jp: 本日より ル･ソベールの経営を任され 社長に就任しました 藤原壮亮と申します。皆さん___ はじめまして
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆さん___ はじめまして
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke greets the staff. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: In the actual line 皆さん is a vocative address — no particle, just a pause/comma. He's calling out to the group, not making them a grammatical subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark them as the subject of はじめまして, but はじめまして is a fixed greeting, not a predicate taking a subject here. を doesn't fit the greeting pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 皆さん、おはようございます。
皆さんがいらっしゃった。

prompt.context_jp: 素性の分からない相手と 契約を続けること___ 双子製菓としても容認できません
prompt.prompt_jp: 契約を続けること___ 双子製菓としても容認できません
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke frames what the company cannot accept. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は sets up 'continuing the contract' as the topic being judged. He's not reporting a new event but making a policy statement about this specific action.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new info being identified ('it turns out that continuing is unacceptable'), which doesn't match his deliberate, declarative tone. に doesn't fit the direct-object slot of 容認できません.

prompt.context_jp: ママじゃなくて 先に匿名のショコラティエ___ 切られるべきでしょ
prompt.prompt_jp: 先に匿名のショコラティエ___ 切られるべきでしょ
prompt.prompt_en: Kō argues who should be cut first, not Mama. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が carries exhaustive-listing force: 'it's the Anonymous Chocolatier (not Mama) who should be cut first.' Kō is singling out exactly who the correct target is.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the pointed identification; the whole point is to pick out this one entity in contrast to Mama. を doesn't fit the passive 切られる.

contrast_examples.en: As for him, he's the culprit. (topic framing)

prompt.context_jp: 真っ先に声をあげたの___ やはり納得のいかない航だった
prompt.prompt_jp: 真っ先に声をあげたの___ やはり納得のいかない航だった
prompt.prompt_en: The narration identifies who spoke up first. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The cleft structure 「〜のは Xだ」 ('the one who did X was Y') uses は to mark the nominalized clause as the topic being identified. This is the standard focus-cleft pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would be ungrammatical in a cleft; the pattern Xのは Yだ requires は. を doesn't fit this copular predication.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に来たのは彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who came first was him. (cleft は)

prompt.context_jp: 母の声___ もう返ってこない
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の声___ もう返ってこない
prompt.prompt_en: The narration describes what will never come back. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は frames 母の声 as the topic — the enduring absence being commented on, with implicit contrast (other things may return, but her mother's voice will not). This fits the reflective narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would report her mother's voice not returning as a new event, but the narration is describing an ongoing state the reader already understands. を doesn't fit the intransitive 返ってくる.

contrast_examples.en: The reply (topic) won't come anymore. (settled state)

prompt.context_jp: 役員の顔___ 若造がまた何か仕掛けてくるのかというような警戒の色が浮かんでいる
prompt.prompt_jp: 役員の顔___ ...警戒の色が浮かんでいる
prompt.prompt_en: Where does the wariness surface? Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 浮かぶ (to surface/appear) takes に for the location where something appears — the surface on which it emerges. 顔に浮かぶ is the fixed collocation; は adds topic/contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks an activity location, but 浮かぶ is about appearing ON a surface, not performing an action there. をは is not a valid particle combo.

contrast_examples.en: A smile surfaces on the face. (に = surface)
Play at the park. (で = activity location)

prompt.context_jp: だとしたら 私___ル･ソベールの経営を 任せてもらえないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ル･ソベールの経営を 任せてもらえないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke asks to be entrusted with Le Sauveur. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 任せる (to entrust) marks the person entrusted with に — the recipient of the responsibility. 'Entrust management TO me' = 私に経営を任せる.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is already used for 経営 (the thing entrusted); 任せる takes two arguments with different particles. が would make 私 the subject, but Sōsuke is the recipient, not the giver, of the entrustment.

contrast_examples.en: Entrust the shop to the son. (に = recipient)

prompt.context_jp: 文子夫人が双子製菓の株式 1.25％___ 取得すること
prompt.prompt_jp: 文子夫人が双子製菓の株式 1.25％___ 取得すること
prompt.prompt_en: What does Mrs. Fumiko acquire? Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 取得する is a transitive verb meaning 'to acquire,' and the thing acquired is the direct object marked by を. The subject (文子夫人) is already marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: が is already used for 文子夫人; a single clause normally has one が-subject. に would mark a goal/location, which doesn't fit 'acquire shares.'

contrast_examples.en: A right arose. (が = subject of intransitive)

prompt.context_jp: 矢継ぎ早の問い___、ハナは唇を噛んだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 矢継ぎ早の問い___、ハナは唇を噛んだ
prompt.prompt_en: Hana reacts to the rapid questions. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the stimulus/trigger that Hana reacts to — 'in response to the rapid questions, she bit her lip.' This is に's reaction/target use.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the questions the subject, but Hana (not the questions) is who acts. で could mean 'by means of/at,' which doesn't match reacting to a stimulus.

contrast_examples.en: I was surprised at his words. (に = stimulus)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の言葉が心に残った。
contrast_examples.en: His words stayed in my heart. (が = subject)

prompt.context_jp: 送信ボタンが押された瞬間、遠く離れた小部屋の画面にも同じ文面が届いた。ハナの指___、キーの上で凍りついた
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナの指___、キーの上で凍りついた
prompt.prompt_en: The dramatic moment: Hana's finger reacts. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が marks Hana's finger as the subject of a vivid, new event the narrator is reporting — a sudden observable moment. Narrative descriptions of noticed events typically use が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the finger as a topic being commented on, losing the dramatic 'and in that moment' punch. を doesn't fit the intransitive 凍りつく.

contrast_examples.en: As for his hand, it was trembling. (topic/background)

prompt.context_jp: 歩き出そうとした瞬間、背後___ 人の気配を感じて肩が跳ねる
prompt.prompt_jp: 背後___ 人の気配を感じて
prompt.prompt_en: Where does Hana sense a presence? Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the location where the presence exists/is sensed — 'a presence BEHIND her.' 〜に気配を感じる is the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would suggest an activity location (where something is being done), but 気配 is a state of existence, not an action. を doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.en: A voice comes from behind. (で = occurrence site)

prompt.context_jp: 彼___ 自分が他の人より偉いと思うようなそぶりを、決して見せまいと意識していた
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___ 自分が他の人より偉いと思うようなそぶりを、決して見せまいと意識していた
prompt.prompt_en: The narration describes Sōsuke's conscious stance. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 彼は sets Sōsuke as the topic for a sustained character-description sentence. The narrator is explaining his habitual stance, not reporting a new event.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would highlight him as new/identified information, but he's already the established referent. The embedded clause already uses 自分が for the lower subject.

contrast_examples.en: He is a kind person. (topic — character trait)

prompt.context_jp: リスクよりも得るもののほうが 多いと___
prompt.prompt_jp: リスクよりも得るもののほうが 多いと___
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke respectfully presents his view to the executives. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: In a formal boardroom pitching to senior executives, 思います (polite form) is required. Sōsuke is deliberately maintaining respectful register despite pushing back.
feedback.incorrect_en: 思う is plain form, too casual for addressing executives. 思っちゃう is colloquial and would sound disrespectful in this high-stakes business meeting.

prompt.context_jp: 営業再開へ向けて 皆様の___を 頂きたいと思います
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆様の___を 頂きたいと思います
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke asks for everyone's support formally. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: お力添え is the formal, humble expression for 'support/assistance' used in business speeches when asking for cooperation. It fits Sōsuke's respectful first-day greeting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手伝い is too casual and physical ('a hand with chores'). 助け is plainer and often implies rescue/urgent aid, mismatched with a polite business request.

contrast_examples.jp: お力添えをお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: I ask for your kind support. (business)

prompt.context_jp: 匿名のショコラティエ様の ご協力が___であると 認識しております
prompt.prompt_jp: ご協力が___であると 認識しております
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke stresses the chocolatier's cooperation is essential. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 不可欠 ('indispensable') is a formal, business-register word that conveys 'cannot do without.' It matches the elevated tone of 認識しております in a business email.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大事 (important) is correct meaning but too casual/general for formal business writing. 必要 (necessary) is weaker — merely needed, not indispensable — and less formal than 不可欠.

prompt.context_jp: 対面で打ち合わせをして 契約___を お願いするつもりです
prompt.prompt_jp: 契約___を お願いするつもりです
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke plans to end the chocolatier's contract. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 契約解除 is the fixed legal/business noun for 'contract termination.' Sōsuke is speaking formally about an official business process.
feedback.incorrect_en: やめ is a casual/plain nominalization, not used in business contracts. 切り is colloquial ('cut off') and lacks the formal legal register of 解除.

contrast_examples.jp: 契約解除をお願いします。

prompt.context_jp: でも これ以上 引きこもりの生活はしたくなくて ___を出してメールしました
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を出してメールしました
prompt.prompt_en: Hana describes what she had to summon to send the email. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 勇気を出す ('to summon courage') is the set collocation for pushing past fear. Hana has scopophobia and reaching out takes genuine courage, not just energy.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気を出す means 'cheer up / be energetic,' which doesn't fit overcoming fear. 力を出す ('exert strength') is physical effort, not emotional bravery.

contrast_examples.jp: 勇気を出して告白した。

prompt.context_jp: 心がつらい時は いつも ここのチョコレートで ___もらったんです
prompt.prompt_jp: ここのチョコレートで ___もらったんです
prompt.prompt_en: Hana describes what the chocolates did for her heart. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 癒やす is the specific verb for soothing/healing emotional pain — the gentle 'balm' meaning. Hana is describing comfort for a hurting heart, exactly the 癒やし nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 直す means 'fix/repair,' used for broken objects or illnesses, not emotional comfort. 助ける ('rescue/help') is too active and situational for the quiet healing she describes.

contrast_examples.en: I was soothed by music. (emotional healing)

prompt.context_jp: 双子製菓が学ぶべきものは___とある
prompt.prompt_jp: 学ぶべきものは___とある
prompt.prompt_en: The narration says there's a huge amount to learn. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 山とある is a set idiom meaning 'there is a mountain of ~' — i.e., a large quantity. It's the standard Japanese metaphor for abundance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 海 (sea) and 星 (stars) are not used in this fixed quantity idiom in Japanese, though they appear in other metaphors. Only 山 forms the idiom 山とある.

contrast_examples.en: There's a mountain of things to do. (idiom)
There are as many as stars. (different idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 重役室の重い扉の前で、藤原壮亮は一度息を___
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤原壮亮は一度息を___
prompt.prompt_en: Sōsuke steadies himself before entering. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 息を整える ('to steady one's breath') is the set phrase for composing oneself before a tense moment — exactly what Sōsuke does before entering the boardroom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を止める means 'hold one's breath,' a physical reflex, not composure. 息を吸う ('inhale') is a single action and lacks the 'collect yourself' nuance 整える provides.

contrast_examples.jp: 息を整えて話し始めた。
contrast_examples.en: Steadied his breath and started talking. (composure)

prompt.context_jp: Sōsuke introducing himself to Le Sauveur's staff on his first day as president.
prompt.prompt_en: Which self-introduction sounds most natural for a new company president greeting staff?

choices.text: 本日より ル･ソベールの経営を任され 社長に就任しました 藤原壮亮と申します
今日から ル･ソベールの経営やることになった 藤原壮亮です
今日より ル･ソベールを経営する 藤原壮亮だ

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses formal register (本日より, 任され, 就任しました, 申します) appropriate for an executive's first greeting. The humble 申します and passive 任され convey proper business etiquette.
feedback.incorrect_en: B mixes casual 今日から and やることになった with です — too flat for a president's debut. C uses plain-form だ, which is far too blunt and would be inappropriate for addressing new subordinates.

prompt.context_jp: Sōsuke emailing the Anonymous Chocolatier to request an urgent meeting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing sounds most natural for a formal business email to an unknown vendor?

choices.text: 至急 対面での打ち合わせを お願いできませんでしょうか？
すぐに会って話したいんですけど いいですか？
早く会おう。都合はどう？

feedback.correct_en: A uses layered polite forms (至急, 対面での, お願いできませんでしょうか) that soften a demanding request. The double-negative question is the standard business way to make urgent asks respectfully.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is conversational and too direct for a first email to an unknown partner. C uses casual plain forms (会おう, どう) that would be rude in business correspondence.

contrast_examples.jp: お願いできませんでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: Might I ask you? (very polite request)
Can you do me a favor? (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Kō is angrily protesting to Sōsuke about Mama being forced out.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for an upset young employee pushing back?

choices.text: なんで ママが辞めなきゃいけないんだよ 納得いかないんだけど！
なぜ ママ様がお辞めにならなければならないのでしょうか
どうして ママさんは辞めるのですか

feedback.correct_en: A matches Kō's emotional, informal protest with 〜なきゃいけないんだよ and 〜んだけど — casual, assertive, and frustrated. Fits a young employee speaking out of anger.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses excessive keigo (お辞めになる, ママ様) that would never apply to one's own colleague-boss in protest. C is grammatically polite but emotionally flat — too neutral for the angry context.

contrast_examples.jp: 納得いかないんだけど！

prompt.context_jp: Hana explaining what the shop's chocolates meant to her.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'the chocolates healed me when my heart was hurting'?

choices.text: 心がつらい時は いつも ここのチョコレートで 癒やしてもらったんです
心が痛い時に チョコレートで治してもらいました
心苦しい時 チョコで修理してもらいました

feedback.correct_en: A pairs 心がつらい (heart hurting) with 癒やす (soothe) — a natural, well-known collocation for emotional comfort. The 〜てもらう frame expresses receiving that comfort.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 治す ('cure/fix') which collocates with illness or objects, not emotional pain — sounds mechanical. C's 修理 ('repair') is for machines, utterly wrong for feelings.

prompt.context_jp: Sōsuke entering the executives' room to request a meeting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening sounds most natural when entering a senior executive's office?

choices.text: 失礼します 少し よろしいでしょうか
お邪魔します ちょっといい？
こんにちは 時間ある？

feedback.correct_en: 失礼します is the standard business entry phrase, and よろしいでしょうか is the polite 'may I?' question. Together they fit asking senior executives for their time.
feedback.incorrect_en: B mixes polite お邪魔します with casual ちょっといい? — inconsistent and too familiar. C's こんにちは and 時間ある? are casual greetings never used entering an executive office.
